title: Captain Tilak: Varma Gets India A Armband as Sooryavanshi Earns Call-Up for Sri Lanka Tri-Series
excerpt: The BCCI's 15-member squad for the June ODI tri-series in Dambulla and Galle puts India's most exciting young talent on a fast track to senior cricket
body:
The Board of Control for Cricket in India has handed Tilak Varma the India A captaincy for the upcoming ODI tri-series in Sri Lanka — a decision that signals the selectors' growing faith in the 22-year-old left-hander as a future leader of Indian cricket.

The series, running from June 9 to 21, will see India A face Sri Lanka A and Afghanistan A across matches in Rangiri Dambulla and Galle. Riyan Parag has been named vice-captain.

## The Squad: Youth Meets Ambition

The 15-member squad reads like a who's who of Indian cricket's next generation. The headline inclusion is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the 15-year-old Rajasthan Royals sensation who has electrified IPL 2026 with his fearless stroke play. The tri-series is being viewed as a critical assessment of Sooryavanshi's readiness for senior international cricket — a graduation that many believe is a matter of "when," not "if."

Alongside the teenaged prodigy, the selectors have picked IPL regulars and domestic standouts including Priyansh Arya, Anshul Kamboj, and several emerging spin-bowling all-rounders. The squad balances proven IPL performers with players who have excelled in domestic white-ball tournaments.

## Why Tilak?

Tilak Varma's elevation to the captaincy, ahead of more senior India A contenders, is a reward for a remarkable 18-month stretch. In IPL 2026, his 75 against Punjab Kings on a treacherous Dharamsala pitch — a knock of control and maturity on a surface where others floundered — was widely cited as one of the innings of the tournament. His overall IPL record for Mumbai Indians this season has cemented his status as one of the most dependable middle-order batters in Indian cricket.

Beyond the numbers, Varma carries the kind of quiet authority that selectors prize. He doesn't court controversy. He doesn't chase the camera. He bats with the composure of someone who has been doing this for a decade, not three years. The captaincy is a test of whether that temperament can extend to tactical leadership and man-management.

## Sooryavanshi's Audition

If Tilak's appointment is a statement about the present, Sooryavanshi's selection is a bet on the future. The teenager from Muzzafarpur, Bihar, became the youngest player to score a century in IPL history this season. His technique against pace — feet moving early, head still, bat coming through in a clean arc — has drawn comparisons to Sachin Tendulkar's early years. Not since Tendulkar himself debuted at 16 has an Indian teenager generated this level of anticipation.

The tri-series offers the BCCI a lower-stakes environment to evaluate how Sooryavanshi handles the rhythm of 50-over cricket and the mental demands of multi-match tours. If he performs in Dambulla and Galle, it would be difficult to keep him out of India's senior squad for the home season later in the year.

## The Hampshire Twist

Adding intrigue to Tilak Varma's summer, Hampshire County Cricket Club has signed the Hyderabad batter for a short stint from June 18 to August 2. He will play four four-day games for the English county — a move designed to sharpen his red-ball skills ahead of India's Test commitments. Varma's 1,204 first-class runs at an average above 50 suggest he has the technique for longer formats, but English conditions will pose a different challenge.

The Sri Lanka tour, followed immediately by a stint in English county cricket, amounts to an intensive three-month boot camp that could define Tilak Varma's trajectory.

## The Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora in Sri Lanka, the UK, and beyond, this squad announcement carries a dual charge. NRI cricket fans in England will have the rare opportunity to watch Tilak Varma in county cricket this summer — live, in person, at the Rose Bowl. And for the global Indian fanbase that has followed Sooryavanshi's IPL breakout through streaming services and social media, the tri-series is the next chapter of a story they have been tracking since the Under-19 World Cup.

## What's Next

India A's first match is scheduled for June 9 at Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium. The final of the tri-series is on June 21. Two multi-day matches against Sri Lanka A in Galle will follow the white-ball leg, offering a broader assessment of the squad's depth.
